title: EFFECT OF WARM/COOL WHITE LIGHTS ON VISUAL PERCEPTION AND MOOD IN WARM/COOL COLOR ENVIRONMENTS
research_question: To investigate the simultaneous effects of warm/cool white light (3000K vs. 6500K) on visual perception and mood in a simulated workspace with different wall colors (white, red, blue).

participants.description: 33 healthy male participants, 24.66 ± 3.29 years old (range 21–35 years old), from Hamadan University of Medical Sciences, Iran.
participants.recruitment: Participants were recruited based on inclusion criteria: lack of definite evening or morning chronotype (MEQ), no eye diseases, no color blindness (Ishihara test), no neurological, cardiovascular, autoimmune, and pulmonary diseases, non-smoking, non-alcohol and non-drugs, good general health (GHQ score < 22), no coffee consumption a week before the test, enough and good quality sleep, and waking up at least one hour before the test. Consent form signed.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: A simulated office workspace partitioned into three booths (2.7x2.5x2.5 m). Each booth had walls covered with wood panels in one of three colors: red, white, or blue. Floor covered with brown carpet. Lighting provided by 6 LED panel lights (12W) and 4 LED linear lights (2W) to maintain 500 Lux illuminance. Two Correlated Color Temperatures (CCTs) were used: 3000K (warm white) and 6500K (cool white). Room was shielded from daylight. Ambient conditions controlled (0.15 m/s airflow, 25°C, 50% RH, <45 dB(A) noise).

mechanisms: Neural association of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (IPRGCs) with the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), where blue spectrum and intensity play a major role, for light-induced non-visual responses.
Correlated Color Temperature (CCT) affects visual perception and mood by changing color characteristics due to changes in the spectral reflectance spectrum of surfaces.
Different activity of the autonomic nervous system in people with different personality traits (e.g., introverts, anxious individuals).
Stress effect of the red color.
Gradual adaptation of people to the environment over time, leading to a shift toward equilibrium in descriptive assessments.
implementation_implications: The combination of white wall color with warm white light or blue wall color with cool white light has a more favorable effect on visual perception and people's mood in workplaces.

In visual design of indoor surfaces in buildings and workspaces, blue or white colors (and even red) can be used in combination with cool or warm light, considering individual and personality factors.
Personality traits of individuals should be considered in the design of light and color in indoor spaces.

limitations: Participants were all male, so findings may not generalize to females.
The mental state of subjects was uncontrollable before entering the test session.
It was not possible to fully control the nutritional status of individuals.

paper_metadata.title: Effect of warm/cool white lights on visual perception and mood in warm/cool color environments
paper_metadata.journal: EXCLI Journal : Experimental and Clinical Sciences

journal: EXCLI Journal : Experimental and Clinical Sciences

environmental_features: warm color environment (e.g., red, orange walls)
cool color environment (e.g., blue, green walls)

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Warm colors evoke feelings of warmth and excitement, while cool colors evoke feelings of calmness and spaciousness.

theory_commitments.theory_name: Light Color Temperature Effects on Mood and Cognition
theory_commitments.specific_claim: Cooler light temperatures enhance alertness and cognitive performance, while warmer light temperatures promote relaxation and comfort.

mechanism_chain.description: The paper suggests that light and wall color interact to influence visual perception and mood, potentially through physiological arousal and cognitive appraisal.

steps.from_construct: cool white light / cool wall color

steps.to_construct: altered visual perception (e.g., spaciousness, brightness) and mood (e.g., reduced depression)

steps.from_construct: warm white light / warm wall color

steps.to_construct: altered visual perception (e.g., pleasantness) and mood (e.g., increased positive affect)
